name: Embleon for WooCommerce
author: vprodukter

sections.description:
This plugin is for workwear and similar shops that print or embroider logos in house. You set the print position and its price. Customers pick a colour, enter a quantity for each size, and upload a logo. Each filled size becomes a real WooCommerce variation line (real SKU and stock). Each logo placement becomes its own cart and order line, so packing and accounting see a real SKU.

Nothing is shown on the storefront until Enable is checked under WooCommerce → Embleon, and only on products that have logo printing turned on.

What merchants can do

  • Define a print position (name, price, invoice line name, on/off). Customers upload one logo file, and the position price is charged per garment.
  • Enter position prices the same way you enter product prices. WooCommerce applies the shop currency and tax class. There is no hard-coded tax rate.
  • Map your own size and colour attribute slugs.
  • Choose allowed logo file types (PNG and PDF by default; JPEG and WebP optional) and a maximum upload size.
  • Turn the picker on per product.
  • Download uploaded logos from the order screen. Files are stored privately; they have no public URL.

Cart and checkout

Classic Cart and Checkout are supported. The Cart and Checkout blocks are also supported: logo lines stay in the cart, their quantities cannot be edited or removed on their own, and logo details (position, file, unit price, linked garment) are exposed on the Store API.

Translations

All customer and admin strings are in English and are translation-ready (text domain embleon-for-woocommerce). On WordPress.org installs, translations are delivered automatically through translate.wordpress.org.

Requirements

WordPress 6.2 or later, PHP 8.0 or later, and WooCommerce 8.2 or later. Compatible with high-performance order storage (HPOS).

For a step-by-step setup, see docs/setup-guide.md in the plugin folder.

Pro version

A separate commercial plugin, Embleon Pro, is available from V Produkter. It adds unlimited print positions, multiple logo files, and once-per-order pricing. This plugin works fully on its own.

Privacy

This plugin does not send data to any external service. Uploaded logo files are stored on your own server in a private folder and are only available to shop staff from the order screen.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the embleon-for-woocommerce folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the zip from Plugins → Add New.
  2. Activate the plugin. Activation writes default settings and a private upload directory. It does not create storefront products or change orders. A hidden “Logo print” product (SKU EMBLEON-LOGO) is created the first time it is needed, or when you tick Create or repair the hidden logo product on the settings screen.
  3. Open WooCommerce → Embleon. Edit the print position name and price, then tick Enable.
  4. Edit each product that should offer logo printing. In the Embleon box, tick Enable logo printing on this product.
  5. If your server is Nginx (or PHP’s built-in server), deny public access to wp-content/uploads/embleon-for-woocommerce/private/. Apache and IIS rules are written automatically. See the setup guide.

Requires WordPress 6.2+, PHP 8.0+, and WooCommerce 8.2+.
sections.faq:
Why is nothing visible on the product page?

Either Enable is still off under WooCommerce → Embleon, or logo printing is not turned on for that product. Both must be on.

The picker does not appear on my theme

The picker hooks the standard woocommerce_before_add_to_cart_button action. If your theme or a page builder skips that hook, add the [embleon] shortcode to the product template. Do not use the hook and the shortcode on the same page.

How should I enter position prices?

Enter them the same way you enter product prices in WooCommerce — including tax or excluding tax, as set under WooCommerce → Settings → Tax. WooCommerce then applies the Logo line tax class (Standard by default) and the shop currency.

Can customers remove a logo line from the cart?

No. Logo lines belong to the garments they were added with. Removing or changing the garment quantities updates the logo quantities.

Where do uploaded logos go?

Into a private directory under wp-content/uploads/embleon-for-woocommerce/private/. Files are checked by extension and MIME type, stored under random names, and are not given a public URL. Shop staff can download them from the order screen.

What is removed if I uninstall the plugin?

Only the plugin settings and the stored id of the hidden logo product. Orders, uploaded files, product meta, and the hidden logo product itself are left in place.
sections.changelog:
1.0.5

  • Added an Upgrade to Pro link on the Plugins screen and a short Pro section on the Embleon settings page.

1.0.4

  • First version submitted to WordPress.org.
  • Translations are delivered through translate.wordpress.org.

1.0.0

  • Settings for the print position, tax class, size and colour attributes, file types, upload size, and the hidden logo product.
  • Product-page picker: yes/no, colour, size × quantity grid, print position, secure logo upload, comment.
  • Cart and orders: real variation lines plus a separate logo line. HPOS-compatible order screen with staff logo download.
  • Classic and block Cart/Checkout, including a Store API cart-item extension for logo data.
  • Uploads stored privately with MIME and size checks.

short_description: Logo printing for WooCommerce: prices per placement, a size × quantity grid, and the logo as its own cart line.
